summary: Blocked model host must be a readable error, not an error loop. User micha: 44/44 models.cubric.studio downloads failed with TLS WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER in <200ms while 45/45 github.com downloads succeeded - network-side interception, install and D: layout both fine. Fix three defects for 1.3.1: raw BoringSSL error surfaced with no host or remedy plus an unhandled rejection; installStore FAILED is terminal so the failed->queued retry requeue is rejected and the UI read path sticks on failed for every user; app.getPath('documents') throwing hard-exits at boot despite an existing shared.js fallback. Mirror-host failover is approval-gated, see brief.

Todo -> Doing. User approved all three fixes for a 1.3.1 release: actionable transport-failure error, failed->queued retry transition, and the app.getPath('documents') boot guard. Mirror-host failover stays out of scope pending a separate go-ahead.

Code complete for 1.3.1, staying in DOING - not closed. Landed: transport-error classification with host + remedy routed to a warning toast instead of the Report-on-GitHub dialog; UW failures now carry their reason instead of bare dep ids; store.requeueDep as an explicit retry door that does NOT widen the transition table (reconciler still cannot resurrect); retry now credits the resumable partial so the bar stops running backwards; app.getPath('documents') boot guard; and a mirror-failover mechanism whose marker comparison is path-equal so a host swap resumes the partial rather than scrapping it. 71/71 suites green (transport-error-message 8 new, install-store 29). Version stamped 1.3.1 and notes approved. OPEN: _MODEL_MIRRORS ships EMPTY so failover cannot fire for anyone - enabling it is an approval-gated Cloudflare change; a same-provider mirror is unproven against this user's failure mode (he verified DNS alone is insufficient and only a tunnel works, stream died at 20 percent = deep-packet, not hostname blocking); 1.3.1 not released; nothing verified in a running app.

ROOT CAUSE of why the user still could not generate, found and fixed on master (0a1d2325) and on the 1.3.1 branch. The UW dep set spans TWO hosts - every type:custom_nodes dep is a github.com zip, every engineAsset weight is on models.cubric.studio - but startUniversalWorkflowInstall rejected as soon as any dep failed, and the reject sat ABOVE the custom-node extract/pip/marker step. So his blocked model host discarded a full set of nodes that had downloaded perfectly from GitHub, and since the drift check reads no-folder as missing, boot re-ran the same repair and discarded them again every launch. He ended up with an engine that could not install one node, so generation died on unknown class_type regardless of weights. Fix: the wait resolves with the failure, the nodes that landed install, then it throws; the error carries the modelJob because both engine-provision callers catch it and would otherwise skip finishCustomNodeInstall (both platforms swept). Second half: that failure also LOCKED HIM OUT - repair-deps runs behind the boot gate which releases on engine:ready and NOT engine:error, and the error phase offered only Retry. Repair now separates an outstanding NODE from an outstanding WEIGHT (nodes present = engine:complete, let him in) and the error carries a Continue-without-them escape on a new engine:gate-release event. Also corrected the shipped remedy copy: it led with set-your-DNS-to-1.1.1.1, which this user tested and disproved; it now leads with a VPN. VERIFIED LIVE, not by code reading: an isolated harness ran the real function against a throwaway CUBRIC_ENGINE_ROOT with one github.com node plus one unreachable-host weight. Post-fix - node folder 36 entries, .mpi_node_commit at the pinned SHA, no leftover zip, PASS. Same harness on the pre-fix commit - node folder NO, marker MISSING, leftover zip YES, which is exactly the on-disk fingerprint expected on the reporting user machine. 305/305 suites green on master, 301/301 on the branch, eslint clean, release:check passes, notes re-approved. NOTE the mirror is still empty and still approval-gated - none of this needed it.
